summary.headline: Dhanuka Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% to Rs 483.34 crore and PAT rose 30% to Rs 97.77 crore, helped by a one-off GST refund; FY27 guidance is low double-digit growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 483.34 crore vs Rs 442.02 crore (about 9% growth), with EBITDA of Rs 124.89 crore vs Rs 109.75 crore and PAT of Rs 97.77 crore vs Rs 75.50 crore. Management attributed the record EBITDA margin largely to a sharp rise in GST refund income in Q4 (Rs 14.5 crore of the Rs 29 crore full-year refund), and said Q4 value and volume growth were roughly equal. Management guided FY27 to low double-digit growth, with the Bayer-acquired molecules (India plus rest of world) and biostimulant recovery as the main offsets to the loss of GST refund and biostimulant disruption. Input costs rose 3-5% at basket level in March-April, with pass-through expected to be gradual and largely complete by Q2.

segments.name: Product mix (Q4 FY26 turnover)
segments.commentary: Insecticide 41%, Herbicide 31%, Fungicide 14%, Others 14%. Management said herbicides and fungicides did not show the growth analysts expected.

segments.name: Bayer-acquired molecules (Triadimenol, Iprovalicarb)
segments.commentary: Recognised about Rs 27 crore in FY26 (India Melody Duo); FY27 expected to be roughly double, with management giving a total figure of about Rs 200 crore in FY27 and FY28 for India plus rest of world, though the transcript is unclear on the split.

segments.name: Biostimulants and biologicals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about Rs 70 crore vs Rs 110 crore in FY25, hit by the biostimulant regulation. FY27 target above Rs 130 crore; three new launches planned for June 2026. MYCOR-e SUPER performing well.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low double digits; management said price growth will exceed volume growth by about 2 percentage points.

EBITDA margin expected to decline about 100 bps in FY27, driven by loss of the GST refund and lower net economic benefit; management said gross margin should be maintained at FY26 levels with no expansion.
Q1 price increase about 2%; further 3-4% price increase planned in Q2 to recover raw material inflation.
Dahej revenue forecast for FY27 cut to Rs 75 crore from the earlier Rs 100 crore.
Royalty income from Bayer molecules expected in FY27, but a little lower than FY26.
Management expects June 2026 to be strong for herbicides given the rainfall forecast and higher oilseed and pulse acreage.
capex_capacity: Operates 4 manufacturing facilities and 41 warehouses; Dahej chemical plant to be used for Bayer-acquired molecule manufacturing.
Triadimenol formulation to shift to India in FY27; Iprovalicarb technical production to start by end of FY27; only one molecule's active ingredient to be made in India, the other sourced externally.
Melody Duo introduced in Q2 FY26 and now part of the India portfolio; both Melody variants being formulated in India.
Three biostimulant launches planned for June 2026.
demand_pricing: Input costs: imported raw materials up about 5-6% due to the weaker rupee; indigenous generics up 15-30% for some products; basket-level increase 3-5%. Prices rose over the prior 45-60 days, with some stabilisation in the last 15 days.
Kharif demand: channel pull observed ahead of expected price increases, hard to separate from end-consumer demand; growth over last year so far in April-May.
Acreage: cotton and pulses expected to gain; soybean acreage uncertain; maize flat or slightly lower. Management said it has a strong soybean herbicide and insecticide portfolio.
Rabi 2026 consumption was better than Kharif per management; channel inventory not expected to be elevated.
Bayer molecules overseas: distributor appointments in about 5 countries with advanced talks in 10 more; distributors struggling to hold prices and volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q4 EBITDA margin the highest ever, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it largely to a sharp rise in GST refund income in Q4 (Rs 14.5 crore of the Rs 29 crore FY26 refund); placement sales were similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guidance breakdown for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price growth to exceed volume growth by about 2 percentage points; management cited Rs 40 crore impact from GST refund and net economic benefit loss, offset by biostimulant recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin assumptions for FY27 given input cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin expected to be held at FY26 levels, not expanded; Q1-Q2 to see some pressure, with full-year pass-through and carryover inventory benefit expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the buyback priced at Rs 1,400?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the price is about 25% above the market price of roughly Rs 1,100 at the time of decision.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall sharply in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Field promotion support from principals increased significantly and Dhanuka Doctor expenses declined; management also issued an expense control directive after Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dahej outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 forecast cut to Rs 75 crore from Rs 100 crore; FY26 delivered Rs 50 crore vs Rs 65 crore forecast. Bifenthrin international sales started in one market, with larger-market registrations taking time.

risks_watch: Raw material cost pass-through: Q1-Q2 margin pressure if the Q2 price hike of 3-4% is not realised; Rabi FY27 impact uncertain if prices keep rising.
Bayer molecule ramp-up: distributor execution in overseas markets, with pricing pressure from distributors and registration delays in larger markets.
Dahej plant: repeated shortfalls against forecasts (FY26 Rs 50 crore vs Rs 65 crore) and a further cut for FY27; continued EBITDA losses.
Biostimulant recovery: FY27 target of over Rs 130 crore depends on the June launches and regulatory normalisation.
Management transition and ESOP: the call referred to an ongoing management transition, and the ESOP has no quantified size in the transcript.
Inventory: management said FY26 year-end inventory was significantly higher due to strategic buying after the West Asia crisis and slow-moving weedicides.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and the Bayer molecule opportunity, but cautious on near-term margins and input costs, with management saying Q1-Q2 will see some pressure. Management was open on the Dahej downgrade and the GST refund one-off, though it was evasive on how the Bayer revenue splits between India and rest of world.
key_quotes: Dahej sales on yearly basis, it was actually Rs. 50 crore as against Rs. 41 crore the previous year.
So, in net-net, we are very hopeful of the opinion we will be able to maintain the gross margin.
I am not expecting any expansion in the gross margin in the current financial year.
We are expecting a revenue of more than Rs. 130 crores.

adds.what: Dahej chemical plant repurposed for Bayer-acquired molecule manufacturing (no new capacity size stated)

growth.why: FY27 guided to low double-digit revenue growth (midpoint ~10%), backed partly by price increases (~2% Q1, 3-4% Q2) and Bayer-acquired molecules (~Rs 200 cr total FY27-28 per brief, split unclear), with Dahej FY27 revenue cut to Rs 75 cr and no clear new capacity sized in the call.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin down about 100 bps in FY27 as the Rs 14.5 crore Q4 GST refund (Rs 29 crore FY26) and Rs 40 crore GST/net economic benefit loss roll off; gross margin held at FY26 levels, with no expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dahej plant is being repurposed for Bayer molecule manufacturing and Iprovalicarb technical production starts by end FY27, but no capacity size or capex was stated, and Dahej FY27 revenue is cut to Rs 75 crore from Rs 100 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to low double digits (~10% midpoint) with price growth expected to exceed volume growth by about 2 percentage points, so volume growth is positive but below price; June 2026 herbicide season expected strong.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond repurposing the Dahej plant and no utilisation figure was given; asset-light and existing-plant reuse imply no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guide is low double-digit revenue growth with margin down ~100 bps, and input costs up 3-5% at basket level with pass-through only gradual by Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risk rests on the Q2 3-4% price hike being realised, Dahej already cut once (FY26 Rs 50 crore vs Rs 65 crore forecast), and biostimulant FY27 target of over Rs 130 crore (vs Rs 70 crore FY26) depending on June launches.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three biostimulant launches are planned for June 2026 and the FY27 biostimulant target is over Rs 130 crore vs Rs 70 crore in FY26.

rows.label: Bayer-acquired molecules revenue ramp (India + rest of world)
rows.why: Management gives about Rs 200 crore total for FY27 and FY28 across India and rest of world, with FY27 roughly double FY26's Rs 27 crore, though the split is unclear and overseas distributors are struggling on price and volume.

rows.label: Price increases to recover input inflation
rows.why: Basket input costs are up 3-5% (imported raw materials up 5-6%), and the company has already planned a about 2% Q1 price rise and a further 3-4% in Q2.

rows.label: Dahej plant losses narrowing
rows.why: Dahej FY26 EBITDA loss was Rs 13 crore and FY27 sales are cut to Rs 75 crore from Rs 100 crore, so continued losses are expected rather than a turnaround.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Bayer molecule opportunity and biostimulant recovery, but cautious on Q1-Q2 margins and input costs, and open on the Dahej cut and GST refund one-off; analysts pressed on the margin reset and the Bayer India vs rest-of-world split.
